title: Mississippi cotton harvest reaches 100% as topsoil dries further
excerpt: USDA rated 85% of Mississippi topsoil short or very short of moisture, up from 80% a week earlier. Its Nov. 23 report puts the cotton harvest at 100%.

paragraphs.text: Mississippi’s cotton harvest reached 100% in the week ending Sunday, Nov. 22, as soils grew drier. USDA rated 85% of the state’s topsoil short or very short of moisture, up from 80% a week earlier.

In Pontotoc County, the U.S. Drought Monitor’s Nov. 17 map put 87.77% of the county’s land in extreme drought or worse, including 22.75% in exceptional drought, its most severe category. USDA’s weekly crop report gives the soil and harvest estimates for Mississippi as a whole.

More topsoil fell into the driest category. USDA rated 51% very short, up from 42% a week earlier. Below the surface, 87% of subsoil moisture was rated short or very short, up from 85%. Only 13% of subsoil was rated adequate in the latest report.

Cotton harvest had stood at 99% a week earlier. Mississippi was at 98% at the comparable point last year, and its five-year average was 97%. Farmers statewide had an estimated 6.6 days suitable for fieldwork in the latest week, down from 6.8.
